title: mini-reserve-ops-deck: compact GPU pool health + burst control UX
creator: Lena Morozova
description: Create a compact, re-usable 'Mini Reserve Ops Deck' component for the Redwood Console that surfaces critical GPU pool health metrics, quick autoscale/burst controls, and a cost preview. This ticket covers the UI prototype, interaction patterns, accessibility considerations, and handoff notes for engineering implementation. The deck will be used in: pool list view, pool detail header, and runbook quick-actions. Goal: enable on-call and SRE personas to triage and apply short-term burst changes without leaving the console while preserving safety (hysteresis, soft confirm, audit trail).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Figma prototype v3 linked and annotated with states (normal, near-saturation, degraded, offline).
2) Component supports three control modes: quick-burst (one-click), modal advanced-burst (detailed slider + hysteresis), and autoscale policy shortcut.
3) Cost preview displays estimated delta for burst duration (per-minute estimate) and shows the dominant cost driver (GPU-minutes or fractional instances).
4) Engineering has a clear instrumentation spec: events for burst_initiated, burst_confirmed, burst_cancelled, autoscale_policy_applied.
5) Accessibility: all controls keyboard navigable, color contrast >= 4.5:1 for critical badges, and screen-reader labels present.
6) Usability test (5 participants from SRE and Platform Eng) completed and feedback incorporated for primary flow.
design_notes:
- Layout: compact card 360x140 (desktop) with three zones: KPIs/sparkline, state badge + quick-action, and cost/confirm affordance.
- KPI set: active_jobs, queue_length, p99_latency, node_utilization (heat ring). Sparklines show 1h/6h trend toggles.
- Quick-burst: one-click 'Burst +20%' applies a pre-approved policy. On first use, show a transient confirmation tooltip; subsequent uses use a soft confirm (undo).
- Advanced-burst modal: duration slider, max GPU cap, hysteresis timeout (cooldown) input, and estimated cost. Include toggles for 'charge to project' and 'notify slack channel'.
- Autoscale shortcut: opens pre-populated policy editor with recommended thresholds based on last 7-day distribution.
- Visuals: use existing console tokens (accent teal for healthy, amber for warning, vermilion for critical). Add micro-animations for state changes to draw attention without being distracting.
- Offline edge case: show last-known telemetry timestamp and safe fallback action (drain traffic or scale-to-zero).
decisions:
- Minimal default burst increment set to 20% rather than absolute GPU counts to simplify mental model; ops can use advanced modal for exact GPUs.
- Cost preview uses median per-GPU cost from billing API; product decided not to surface per-region variations in the quick preview to avoid clutter.
- Chose optimistic UI for quick-burst (immediate feedback) but requires background reconciliation and a visible audit item in the pool activity log.
- To avoid permission sprawl, quick-burst is gated by an RBAC scope 'pool.burst.quick'; advanced modal requires 'pool.burst.manage'.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Raj: Prototype looks promising. Need explicit signal for 'stale telemetry' state; otherwise on-call may take unsafe actions. Suggested showing TTL and last sample time.
2025-02-13 — Maya: Add a cost comparison microcopy 'vs baseline' and a link to bill-of-record for finance teams. Keep quick-burst friction low but accountable.
2025-02-14 — Jordan: Iterated mock to include keyboard shortcuts (B to open burst modal). Updated Figma v2 with annotated keyboard flows.

2025-02-16 — Avery: Engineering can support the burst_initiated and burst_confirmed events. Need telemetry payload spec: pool_id, delta_percent, duration_minutes, user_id, request_id. Will add implementation tasks after design sign-off.
2025-02-17 — Maya: Usability testing scheduled 2025-02-19. Focus on SRE task: 'safely apply burst while minimizing escalation'.
2025-02-20 — Hannah: Ran quick pilot with internal canary on test cluster. Observed confusion around 'undo' affordance; recommend explicit 'cancel burst' action in pool activity feed.

1) Incorporate telemetry TTL and explicit stale-state visuals (deadline 2025-02-24).
2) Finalize Figma v3 annotations and handoff package for Eng (component tokens, spacing, microcopy).
3) Create engineering ticket ENG-85671 for instrumentation + API contract.
4) Run 5 usability tests and produce findings doc.
5) Post-launch: enable A/B to test quick-burst default increment (20% vs 30%).

notes_for_engineering:
- Backend: provide endpoints for: preview_cost(pool_id, delta_percent, duration_minutes), initiate_burst(pool_id, delta_percent, duration_minutes, policy_id), cancel_burst(request_id).
- Telemetry: emit events with request_id and correlate with audit log.
- UI should poll health endpoint at 5s for deck when open and gracefully back off to 30s when backgrounded.
- Add feature flag 'mini_ops_deck_v1' for staged rollout.
user_test_plan: Recruit 5 participants: 2 SREs, 2 Platform Engineers, 1 PM. Tasks: 1) Identify pool nearing saturation, 2) Apply quick-burst and observe cost preview, 3) Undo burst, 4) Create advanced burst with cooldown, 5) Validate audit log entry. Collect SUS and task completion time.
implementation_risks:
- Mis-synced telemetry could cause unsafe bursts; mitigated by stale TTL and disabling quick-burst when data older than 90s.
- Cost estimator variance may surprise finance teams; include link to bill-of-record and conservative estimate.
- RBAC gating complexity — need clear mapping from console roles to API scopes.
